title: De legibus Angliae, ca. 1300
shelf_note: Genuine c.1300 manuscript of Bracton (Harvard). It is a major primary source, but English common law sits outside the library's esoteric and early-science shelves, and no tradition or collection is assigned.
structure_note: printed_backsteps 45 of 120 printed numbers most likely come from misread folio numerals, not a scan disorder. On p205 the image's running folio is 'LXXXIX' and the OCR gives 'LXXXIIII'. Pages 203 (recto LXXXVIII), 204 (verso) and 205 (recto LXXXIX) run in the right order.

book_verdict: The scans are the right leaves in the right order, but the OCR of this Gothic legal hand is largely confabulated. On all three pages the opening writs, rubrics and case dates are replaced with plausible Bracton-style Latin. The translations faithfully render that invented text into fluent English, so a reader cannot rely on either pane.

title: 坤輿萬國全圖 (Complete Map of All Lands)
shelf_note: The pages are not Ricci's world map. They are a Ming illustrated chuanqi drama: the block edge reads 題紅記 (Ti hong ji, 'Red Leaf' play), with 第二十齣 'scene 20', character roles 生/旦/丑/貼 and a woodcut. The wrong work sits under the title.
structure_note: The record's identity is wrong (I7). It has 101 page records, and every sampled page is from the Ti hong ji drama, not the 1602 map. The pages are double-leaf spreads photographed open, so each image is one spread.

title: De iureiurando theses XL
shelf_note: A 1581 legal disputation on oaths (Roman law). It is genuine and early modern, but no tradition or collection is assigned, and it is outside the library's esoteric and early-science core.
structure_note: Page 2 is the blank verso of the title leaf with the title showing through in mirror image. It was OCR'd and translated as if it carried text. The other 8 pages and 7 OCR'd pages are consistent with a short pamphlet.

title: De quattuor virtutibus cardinalibus, sive De formula honestae vitae, cum commento [Latin and German verse translation]. Preceded by: Vita Senecae
shelf_note: A 1492 incunable of pseudo-Seneca (Martin of Braga) with Latin commentary and German verse. It is a moral-philosophy primary source; no collection is assigned.
structure_note: Book language is recorded as 'German', but the pages are mainly Latin commentary with short German verse paraphrases. The 4 printed backsteps probably come from misread or absent leaf numerals (p25 carries a manuscript '53'). Counts are otherwise consistent: 53 pages, 53 with OCR, 51 translated.

book_verdict: The right leaves are well read overall, and the German verse is a nice touch. There is nothing serious.

title: 理學類編·卷四~卷六 (vol 2)
shelf_note: Zhang Jiushao's Ming Neo-Confucian compendium (Siku quanshu copy), here on cosmology and fenye astrology. It is a reasonable fit for a natural-philosophy or astrology shelf; the catalogue collection is only 'universallibrary'.
structure_note: Pages 12-14 are consecutive, with leaf numbers 六 and 七 visible and the text continuous. The display_title is null and the published date is 'Unknown'. The page reads Siku quanshu (Qianlong era); nothing else stands out.
